Latest from the Labs

AnAnthropic · 🛠️Claude ShipThree agents for GitHub pull requests: Code Review (generally available), plus PR Steward and Claude Approvals (beta), which can review, fix and approve changes a team's policy allows. For Team and Enterprise plans; a /ship command in Claude Code. Reported via secondary coverage; Anthropic's productivity figures are self-reported.23 Nov 2026 GDGoogle DeepMind · 🔬DeepMind Institute essay: "What comes after AGI?"An essay on the DeepMind Institute site arguing that, as several technological routes toward artificial general superintelligence take shape, the regime beyond AGI is moving from philosophical speculation to empirical research and governance questions. It draws on the technical report "From AGI to ASI"; coverage describes four routes: scaling, paradigm shifts, coordination among many agents, and recursive self-improvement. Institute essays are not presented as Google's official view.19 Nov 2026 GDGoogle DeepMind · 🧠Gemini 4 NeonThe mid-tier Gemini 4 model, between Carbon and Hydrogen, aimed at long, tool-heavy agent work; in Google Antigravity it can coordinate Hydrogen subagents. 1M-token context, four thinking levels, text/image/video/audio/PDF input. In the Gemini API, AI Studio, Gemini for business, Antigravity and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers; a Neon for cyber variant goes to vetted defenders. Reported via news coverage; Google's comparisons with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol are company claims.18 Nov 2026 AnAnthropic · 🏢Anthropic prices its IPOAnthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the target range, with Nasdaq trading under the symbol ANT from 19 November. Reports differ on the total raised and the valuation.18 Nov 2026 OAOpenAI · 🧠GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 SolOpenAI's update to its two GPT-6 lines: Astra for demanding professional work in science, law and finance, Sol as the cheaper everyday model. Available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for paid plans and in the API. OpenAI reports Astra +6.2 points over its predecessor on GDPval v2 with 22% fewer output tokens and a lower API price; coverage says Astra is OpenAI's first externally released model rated High for AI self-improvement under its own framework. Figures are OpenAI's claims.17 Nov 2026 MSMicrosoft AI · 🧠MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 FlashMicrosoft's in-house coding models announced at Ignite and rolled into GitHub Copilot; part of a wider set of MAI models including MAI Cyber 2 Flash. Reported via secondary coverage; price-performance claims are Microsoft's.17 Nov 2026 QwAlibaba Qwen · 🧠Qwen4-MaxAlibaba's new flagship after a limited preview: a sparse mixture-of-experts model reported at 2.4T total and 71B active parameters, native vision and a 1M-token context. API only, no weights; Alibaba says smaller Qwen4 models will be open-sourced later. Alibaba reports about 60% lower cost per task than its predecessor on its own benchmark. Figures from secondary coverage.16 Nov 2026 OAOpenAI · 🛠️ChatGPT WalletA payment feature that lets ChatGPT's agents buy things for users with a tokenised card; each purchase is approved with biometrics. US Pro subscribers first.13 Nov 2026 GDGoogle DeepMind · 🧠Gemini 4 HydrogenThe fast, low-cost member of the Gemini 4 family for everyday coding and agent work. It replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash in Search, the Gemini app and developer tools. Google says it scores above Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default thinking level and runs about 2.5 times faster than 3.8 Flash (company claims).12 Nov 2026 MeMeta AI · 🧠Muse EmberMeta Superintelligence Labs' lightest and most cost-efficient Muse model so far, aimed at running agents. Reported via secondary coverage.9 Nov 2026 AnAnthropic · 🧠Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2Anthropic's new top models for hard technical work. Fable 5.2 is generally available; Mythos 5.2 goes only to vetted organisations through Anthropic's life-sciences and cyber verification programmes. Anthropic reports 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2 for Fable 5.2 (Opus 5.5: 62.3%); press coverage also reports lower prices and fewer refusals than Fable 5.1. Benchmark and pricing figures are the company's, as reported. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site.9 Nov 2026 OAOpenAI · 🧠GPT-6 CyberA cybersecurity-focused version of GPT-6 Astra, limited to approved customers in OpenAI's Daybreak Red programme. The AI Compute Stack: From Electrons to Tokens
What it physically takes to run AI: power, factories, chips, memory and the economics that tie them together. Power → private energy → factories → vs supercomputers → cooling & water → chips → supply chain → networks → memory → custom silicon → inference → edge devices → token prices → financing → China → frontier sites → economics → the horizon. Each part stands alone; together they explain why AI is now an energy and hardware story as much as a software one.

11 · Build a Company

Three Lanes, Three Very Different Bets

Every AGI-adjacent startup — and increasingly, every researcher's career choice — falls into one of three strategic lanes.

🔴
Lane 1 — Frontier Scale-First
Training your own foundation model from scratch. Capital-intensive, research-credibility-gated, and the slowest feedback loop of the three.
Explore Lane 1 →
 🔵
Lane 2 — Applied & Agentic Layer
Building on top of existing frontier models. Fast shipping cadence, flat teams, and the most legible path to revenue.
Explore Lane 2 →
 🟢
Lane 3 — Narrow Research Bet
A small, senior team betting everything on one research thesis. No product, no revenue plan — just conviction and capital.
Explore Lane 3 →

Analyst view · Aug 2026

Where AI Sits on Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle

Gartner's yearly map of how far each AI technology is from everyday, productive use. AI agents and sovereign AI are at the peak of the hype; generative AI is at the bottom of the trough and expected to reach the plateau within two years; artificial general intelligence is the only item put more than ten years out. Gartner's framing for 2026: the question has moved from "can we build with AI?" to "can we account for what our AI does and what it costs?"

Innovation Trigger 16

  • AI Observability 5–10 yrs
  • AI Factories 5–10 yrs
  • Quantum for AI 5–10 yrs
  • Agentic Commerce 5–10 yrs
  • First-Principles AI 2–5 yrs
  • AI Cybersecurity Governance 2–5 yrs
  • Physical AI 5–10 yrs
  • Causal AI 2–5 yrs
  • AI Agent Identity 2–5 yrs
  • AI Simulation 5–10 yrs
  • AI Governance Technologies 5–10 yrs
  • AI-Native Software Engineering 5–10 yrs
  • Artificial General Intelligence >10 yrs
  • Composite AI <2 yrs
  • Decision Intelligence 2–5 yrs
  • FinOps for AI 2–5 yrs

Peak of Inflated Expectations 4

  • Sovereign AI 2–5 yrs
  • AI Engineering 2–5 yrs
  • AI Agents 2–5 yrs
  • Multimodal AI 2–5 yrs

Sliding into the Trough 4

  • World Models 2–5 yrs
  • AI-Ready Data 2–5 yrs
  • Foundation Models <2 yrs
  • Synthetic Data 2–5 yrs

Trough of Disillusionment 2

  • Edge AI <2 yrs
  • Generative AI <2 yrs

Slope of Enlightenment 1

  • Knowledge Graphs 2–5 yrs

Timings = Gartner's estimate of years to the plateau, read from its published 2026 chart. Positions and timings are Gartner's opinion, not measured data; the curve and dot positions above are our own drawing, placed by reading Gartner's published chart (approximate), not Gartner's graphic. Links go to where this site covers the topic. Gartner also reports that only 17% of organisations have deployed AI agents so far and expects more than 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027. Source: Gartner, "Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence, 2026".
